candidate.educational_objective: Respond safely to signs of promethazine injection–related tissue injury.

options.A: Continue the infusion because local pain is an expected benign effect.
options.B: Stop the infusion immediately and evaluate the site for possible extravasation or arterial injury.
options.C: Increase the infusion rate to shorten tissue exposure.
options.D: Apply pressure and restart the same infusion through the affected site.

candidate.rationale: Promethazine injection can cause severe tissue injury, including necrosis and gangrene, after extravasation or inadvertent intra-arterial exposure. Current labeling directs immediate discontinuation of the infusion if a client reports pain at the injection site during IV administration and evaluation for arterial injection or perivascular extravasation.
candidate.source_claim_supported: IV promethazine may cause severe tissue injury; injection-site pain during IV infusion requires immediate discontinuation and evaluation.
candidate.source_locator: Boxed Warning / Warnings—Severe Tissue Injury; IV administration—pain at injection site requires immediate discontinuation and evaluation
candidate.stem: During an IV promethazine infusion, a client reports intense burning and pain at the infusion site and swelling is noted. What is the nurse’s priority action?
